    What's included

    We didn't build a clubhouse to sit empty. We put the money in the walls.

    No pool. No gym. No amenity fee. No nonsense. You'll never pay for a pool you don't swim in — and why would you swim in a pool when Tahoe is thirty minutes up the hill? Everything you pay for here is behind your own locked door.

    Your own garage

    Roughly 11′ × 21′, opening into your own entry. Park, unload, done. No scraping ice off anything.

    Laundry in the home

    Full-size hookups inside your home. No shared machines. No quarters. No hallway.

    Gas cooking

    A gas range in every kitchen. Dishwasher, disposal and pantry standard.

    Your own thermostat

    Your thermostat. Your meter. Nobody else's setting.

    Nobody lived here first

    New appliances, new systems, new windows. You are the first tenant this home has ever had.

    Fire sprinklers throughout

    Every home sprinklered and fire-separated from its neighbors. Safer — and a lot quieter.

    One accessible home

    The Ponderosa, 515-101. Step-free approach, wide doors, roll-in shower, real turning room. December 1, 2026. There is only one.

    Your own front door

    No lobby. No corridor. No shared entry. You park, you walk in, and the day is over.

    Vaulted upper homes

    Great rooms and kitchens vaulted to the roofline, windows on three sides.

    Furnished · February to June 2027

    The Session Lease

    The 84th Nevada Legislature convenes February 1, 2027 and runs 120 days. Our two largest homes are finished January 1 — four weeks ahead of it — and both can be leased furnished and move-in ready.

    If you're here on session, on an agency contract, on a hospital assignment, or running a Northern Nevada territory out of a Reno hotel — you already know what four months of hotel rooms costs, and what it costs you at the end of the day. This is the other option.

    • Furnished top to bottom. Beds, seating, table, kitchen, linens. Bring a suitcase and a laptop.
    • 1,539 to 1,567 square feet. Three bedrooms, two baths. Room to work and room to have someone stay.
    • Your own entry and your own garage. No lobby, no front desk, nobody logging when you come in.
    • Laundry in the home. Not down a hall, not in a basement, not with a card.
    • Five minutes to the Legislative Building. About two miles to the Capitol complex and downtown.
    • 90-day minimum. Session length, contract length, or the whole year — your call.
    Reserve a Session Lease See the Sugar Pine plan

    Furnished rates are quoted per home and per term. There is no posted number, because a four-month furnished lease and a twelve-month unfurnished one are not the same product and shouldn't carry the same price.

    The homebase

    Load the truck. Lock it. Go.

    You didn't move to Northern Nevada to sit in an apartment.

    Tahoe is thirty minutes. Reno is forty. Virginia City, the Carson Valley and the Sierra passes are all inside an hour. Trailheads start twelve minutes from your front door.

    Your skis, your bike, your packs and your truck live in your own garage — not in a storage unit across town, not in a numbered space you fight for on a Sunday night. The mountains don't have parking for your truck. We do.

    Sage & Stafford is somewhere to leave from.

    The city

    Come for what Nevada doesn't take. Stay for what Carson City doesn't ask.

    No state income tax. No one in your business. 58,000 people in a valley with the Sierra on one side and high desert on the other, a nineteen-minute commute, and Tahoe half an hour up the hill. People arrive for the math. They stay because it's the last place that still lets you be left alone.

    2.7%Market vacancy. Nothing sits empty here.
    0%State income tax
    19minAverage commute
    300Sunny days a year
    2miTo the State Capitol
    30minTo Lake Tahoe
    Schools

    Nobody gets bussed across a county

    Six elementary schools, two middle schools and Carson High, all on one compact footprint. Carson City School District runs career programs in health sciences, trades and culinary that put graduates to work in this valley.

    Weekends

    Trails start where the pavement ends

    Prison Hill puts you on a ridge over town in twenty minutes. Ash and Kings Canyon climb into pine and running water. Carson River stays flat for a stroller. No parking pass, no two-hour drive — shoes and ten minutes.

    Community

    Something on every weekend

    Farmers markets, car shows on Carson Street, summer live music, and Nevada Day — the state's birthday parade, hosted here since 1938, which shuts main street down for a Saturday. Check the events calendar.

    Nineteen-minute commute

    State offices, the hospital, the schools and the industrial park all sit inside fifteen minutes. That's an hour a day you don't spend on a freeway.

    No income tax. State or local.

    On a household making $90,000, that is real money in the account every month — on top of a cost of living under Reno's and far under California's.

    About 300 sunny days

    High desert at 4,700 feet. Dry air, clear winters, summers that cool off at night. Snow falls and then goes.

    Tahoe 30 min. Reno 40.

    Virginia City, the Carson Valley and the Sierra passes are all inside an hour. Small town, none of the trade-offs.

    Jobs that don't disappear

    State government anchors it; healthcare and manufacturing have grown around it. Unemployment below the national rate. Not a boom town — a stable one.

    A dozen-plus parks

    Plus Mills Park — miniature railroad, ball fields, the fairgrounds. A game of catch is a five-minute decision, not an expedition.

    A real Western downtown

    Capitol grounds, the old Mint that's now the state museum, brick storefronts, a brewpub, the V&T Railroad. Mark Twain started writing here.

    Neighbors you'll actually meet

    Kids outside. People wave. Plenty who came for one year are still here ten years later.

    Two minutes, one form
